'''Benjamin Klaas Selinger''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|AM}} (born 23 January 1939) is an Australian chemist, for many years a professor with the chemistry department of the [[Australian National University]], later head of department and Professor Emeritus. He is perhaps best known as a consumer advocate and author. His ''Chemistry in the Marketplace'', first published in 1968, is from June 2017 in its sixth edition.<ref name=Eureka/>

==History==
Selinger was born in Sydney, the eldest son of German-Jewish refugees Hilde Selinger (died 19 May 1994)<ref name=AJN1994>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article261706397 |title=Advertising |newspaper=[[The Australian Jewish News]] |volume=99 |issue=36 |location=New South Wales, Australia |date=27 May 1994 |access-date=4 July 2023 |page=17 (Life/Style) |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref> and Herbert Selinger (died 1973).<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article263125241 |title=Family Notices |newspaper=[[The Australian Jewish Times]] |volume=81 |issue=8 |location=New South Wales, Australia |date=15 November 1973 |access-date=4 July 2023 |page=24 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref> His father, who was naturalized as an Australian citizen in 1944,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article128393776 |title=Advertising |newspaper=[[The News (Adelaide)]] |volume=42 |issue=6,382 |location=South Australia |date=12 January 1944 |access-date=4 July 2023 |page=5 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article232756338 |title=Certificates of Naturalization |newspaper=[[Commonwealth of Australia Gazette]] |issue=197 |location=Australia, Australia |date=5 October 1944 |access-date=4 July 2023 |page=2262 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref> was an electrical engineer and lecturer at the [[N.S.W. University of Technology]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article261720715 |title=Socially Yours |newspaper=[[The Australian Jewish Times]] |volume=61 |issue=42 |location=New South Wales, Australia |date=15 April 1955 |access-date=4 July 2023 |page=4 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref> He is credited with inculcating in his son the need to investigate the workings of things.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://chemaust.raci.org.au/article/marchapril-2020/cat%E2%80%99s-whisker.html |title=From a Cats Whisker |magazine=Chemistry in Australia |issue=March–April 2020 |access-date=4 July 2023 |archive-date=9 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240409182957/http://chemaust.raci.org.au/article/marchapril-2020/cat%E2%80%99s-whisker.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He grew up in the Sydney suburb of [[Oatley, New South Wales|Oatley]],<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article261411141 |title=Letters |newspaper=[[The Sydney Jewish News]] |volume=XIII |issue=44 |location=New South Wales, Australia |date=5 September 1952 |accessdate=4 July 2023 |page=9 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref> and was educated at [[Mortdale|Mortdale Public School]] and [[Sydney Boys' High School]].<ref name=encyclopedia/> After completing his (then compulsory) National Service training he enrolled at the [[University of Sydney]], graduating in 1960 with an Honours degree in [[surface chemistry]]. He achieved his Masters degree in [[Electron paramagnetic resonance|electron spin resonance spectroscopy]] in 1961. He spent two years as a teaching Fellow at Sydney University, then earned his PhD 1962–1964 at the [[University of Stuttgart]].<ref name=encyclopedia/>

In 1973, he was appointed a member of the Food Standards Committee of the [[National Health and Medical Research Council]] (NHMRC).<ref name=encyclopedia/>

In 1973, he became associated with the [[Australian Consumers Association]], publishers of ''[[Choice (Australian magazine)|Choice]]'' magazine,<ref name=golden>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article262893391 |title=Science is golden for professor |newspaper=[[The Australian Jewish News]] |volume=114 |issue=19 |location=New South Wales |date=2 February 2007 |access-date=3 July 2023 |page=17 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref> elsewhere cited as a twelve-year involvement 1960s–1970s.<ref name=encyclopedia>{{cite book|url=https://www.eoas.info/biogs/P002588b.htm |title=Encyclopedia of Australian Science and Invention: Selinger, Benjamin Klaas (1939 - )|publisher=Swinburne University of Technology |year=1997}}</ref>

He had a particular interest in forensic science, critical of the way scientific evidence is produced in court.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article125001761 |title=Courtroom science |newspaper=[[The Canberra Times]] |volume=58 |issue=17,722 |location=Australian Capital Territory, Australia |date=6 April 1984 |access-date=3 July 2023 |page=6 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref> and the uncritical acceptance of scientific evidence as produced in the [[Lindy Chamberlain]] trial. He had much to say on the balance of risk versus utility in various materials and substances; the way public opinion and political decision-making could be affected by media interpretation in the cases of [[asbestos]]<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article102034400 |title=Political problem of asbestos |newspaper=[[The Canberra Times]] |volume=62 |issue=19,285 |location=Australian Capital Territory, Australia |date=25 July 1988 |access-date=4 July 2023 |page=2 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref> and [[2,4,5-T]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article126163234 |title=ANU study finds no evidence to hold against herbicide |newspaper=[[The Canberra Times]] |volume=55 |issue=16,512 |location=Australian Capital Territory, Australia |date=10 December 1980 |access-date=4 July 2023 |page=24 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref>

==Publications==
===Books===
*Ben Selinger, Russell Barrow ''Chemistry in the Marketplace'' 6th edition June 2017 CSIRO Publishing
<blockquote>"Whether your interest is swimming pools or sunscreen, pharmaceuticals or polymers, or simply a desire to put your chemistry into more familiar contexts, this book has much to offer... the wealth of detailed information is both interesting and enlightening. One could read the book from cover to cover but my view is that its strength lies in its range and detail, making it much more likely to be dipped into when looking for anecdotes or for some facts and figures to brighten up a lesson or create a resource."
Janet Mitchell, School Science Review 99(366), September 2017</blockquote>

===Journals===
As a research scientist, by 1991 he had published 129 papers in science journals.

''The Canberra Times'' published numerous articles on chemistry subjects by Selinger. Longer articles under his [[byline]] include:
*{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article120914257 |title=Dial-a-drunk for Safety |newspaper=[[The Canberra Times]] |volume=63 |issue=19,505 |date=4 March 1989 |page=25 }} (science of the breathalyser)
*{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article120915675 |title=Bursting the Education Bubble |newspaper=[[The Canberra Times]] |volume=63 |issue=19,512 |date=11 March 1989 |page=21}} (university politics and froth)
*{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article122260143 |title=Chemistry, a social performer |newspaper=[[The Canberra Times]] |volume=63 |issue=19,568 |date=6 May 1989 |page=20 }} (teaching and research)
*{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article122267458 |title=Seasoning reveals secrets of soup |newspaper=[[The Canberra Times]] |volume=63 |issue=19,596 |date=3 June 1989 |page=7}} (surface tension and forensic science)
*{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article122272338 |title=Green guide for environmentally-aware consumers |newspaper=[[The Canberra Times]] |volume=63 |issue=19,618 |date=25 June 1989 | page=22 }} (thoughts on controversial subjects)
*{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article127263392 |title=Sniffing out chemical truths |newspaper=[[The Canberra Times]] |volume=70 |issue=21,807 |date=31 December 1994 |page=18}} (review of a book by British counterpart [[John Emsley]])

Articles published in ''Chemistry'' magazine, published by the [[Royal Australian Chemical Institute]], include:
*{{cite web |url=https://chemaust.raci.org.au/article/april-2018/good-measure-beer-and-sunscreen.html |title=A Good Measure of Beer and Sunscreen |date=April 2018 |access-date=2023-07-04 |archive-date=2023-07-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230704061428/https://chemaust.raci.org.au/article/april-2018/good-measure-beer-and-sunscreen.html |url-status=dead }}

*{{cite web |url=https://chemaust.raci.org.au/article/septemberoctober-2018/sticky-and-sugary-solutions-polarising-questions.html |title=Sticky and sugary solutions — Polarising Questions |date=September–October 2018 |access-date=2023-07-04 |archive-date=2023-12-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231204070648/https://chemaust.raci.org.au/article/septemberoctober-2018/sticky-and-sugary-solutions-polarising-questions.html |url-status=dead }}

==Recognition==
In 1991, Selinger was made a Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering]].<ref name=Eureka/>
Later that year he was awarded a [[Eureka Prize]], recognising his contribution to science journalism.<ref name=Eureka>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article122387079 |title=Selinger wins a Eureka prize |newspaper=[[The Canberra Times]] |volume=66 |issue=20,622 |location=Australian Capital Territory, Australia |date=28 September 1991 |accessdate=3 July 2023 |page=17 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref>
He donated the $2000 cash prize to Canberra's Jewish community; it was used to inaugurate the Selinger–Hollander prize, to be awarded annually to the young boy or girl who contributed most to the community during that year.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article261733720 |title=Chanukah in Canberra |newspaper=[[The Australian Jewish News]] |volume=104 |issue=14 |location=New South Wales, Australia |date=25 December 1998 |access-date=4 July 2023 |page=24 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref>

In 1998, he was appointed Professor Emeritus at the Australian National University, Canberra.<ref name=encyclopedia/>

In 2007, he was made a Member of the [[Order of Australia]] (AM).<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article262895666 |title=Shmooze Selinger and Friend |newspaper=[[The Australian Jewish News]] |volume=114 |issue=29 |location=New South Wales, Australia |date=20 April 2007 |accessdate=3 July 2023 |page=2 |via=National Library of Australia}} The title refers to a photograph of Selinger with [[Nicole Kidman]].</ref>

==Other interests==
Selinger and his wife were active in the social life of Canberra's Jewish community — in the 2000s they organised a series of lectures entitled "Beyond the Pale" and a men's group "Grumps R Us".<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article263159085 |title=New Group for Grumpy Old Men |newspaper=[[The Australian Jewish News]] |volume=112 |issue=40 |location=New South Wales, Australia |date=7 July 2006 |accessdate=4 July 2023 |page=7 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref>

==Family==
Selinger married Veronica "Vera"<ref name=AJN1994/> Hollander sometime around 1967<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article107881722 |title=Family Notices |newspaper=[[The Canberra Times]] |volume=40 |issue=11,520 |location=Australian Capital Territory, Australia |date=14 July 1966 |access-date=4 July 2023 |page=28 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref> and had a home in [[Garran, Australian Capital Territory|Garran, A.C.T.]]<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article125629987 |title=Tranquil gardens scene for fair |newspaper=[[The Canberra Times]] |volume=55 |issue=16,468 |location=Australian Capital Territory, Australia |date=27 October 1980 |access-date=4 July 2023 |page=7 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref>
They had two sons, Adam Selinger (born c. 1970) and Michael Jorg Selinger (born 12 January 1973)<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article110702215 |title=Family Notices |newspaper=[[The Canberra Times]] |volume=47 |issue=13,331 |location=Australian Capital Territory, Australia |date=13 January 1973 |access-date=4 July 2023 |page=17 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref>

His younger brother Robert Selinger (born c. 1944)<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article262957809 |title=JNF Acknowledgements |newspaper=[[The Australian Jewish Times]] |volume=73 |issue=7 |location=New South Wales, Australia |date=12 November 1965 |accessdate=4 July 2023 |page=7 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref> was in 2020 awarded the Medal of the Order of Australia for his service to the community through [[Rotary International]], and education — during his 50-year career he taught at, amongst others, [[Chatswood High School]], [[Drummoyne Boys' High School]] and [[Ashfield Boys High School]]<!--don't add apostrophe-->.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22chamber%2Fhansardr%2Ff3ed3760-e998-492f-9f3e-11b9802d8a98%2F0303%22;src1=sm1 |title=Hansard: Australia Day Awards: Statement by the Member for Bennelong |author=John Alexander |author-link=John Alexander (Australian politician) |date=24 February 2020 |access-date=5 July 2023}}</ref>
